items.summary: UKMTO reported Tuesday (17:30 UTC) that a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile off Khasab, Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz; local authorities reported a fire aboard that has since been extinguished, with all crew safe and no environmental impact reported. Regional outlets (Al Arabiya English, Iran International, Gulf News) carried the breaking UKMTO alert; Iran International/Gulf News graphics suggest a second vessel (a container ship) may also have been hit — details still developing. Comes as Iran and Oman discuss a temporary joint shipping corridor.
items.title: New UKMTO warning: tanker struck by unknown projectile in Hormuz on Tuesday — fire out, crew safe

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (statement to Parliament; joint statement released same day)
items.summary: UK PM Andy Burnham told Parliament Monday that the Sept 27 suspected drone/explosives plot at RAF Fairford — the base US bombers used for Iran strikes — was 'highly likely coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by the IRGC'; Britain sanctioned two IRGC-linked men (counterespionage chief Ruhollah Bazghandi and facilitator Shahram Ali Reza Tamarzadeh Jakki). The US State Department released a joint statement the same day with 28 allied governments recognizing the UK's attribution and condemning Iran's covert operations in Europe. Iran rejects any connection (Ambassador Seyed Ali Mousavi via IRNA).
items.title: UK blames IRGC for RAF Fairford plot; 29 nations back the attribution

items.summary: Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, said Monday that Iran and its allies wrongly assessed Gulf Arab countries were 'the weakest link' in the US-Israel war against Iran, posting that 'we are all targeted and that our security is indivisible' and urging joint Gulf action to defend against attacks by Iran and its proxies.
items.title: UAE's Gargash calls for 'joint Gulf action' against Iran and its proxies
